title: the mounted-combat engine site - the R403 charge lands
audit_comment: THE SITE ROUND - the R403 mount layer charges the engine: the Character gains the mount field (the mount actor site), beginCombat reads it (the mounted resolution seam), and the mount layer charge closes with the site. The six feeder seams (R123 movement, R170 followers mounts, R189 charge damage, R321 aerial, R328 cavalier, R356 mount spell) stay pinned in their headers - the site reads the layer contract, it does not re-pin the feeders. The R775 fix carries the regtest R403 condition flips: RT file patches ride the in-memory engine text, so the include and this audit block survive alongside the flipped conditions. ONE PATCH PER FILE this round: the multi-patch chaining class (a file patched twice lost the first flip to the stale re-read - the site design exposed it twice, RT and non-RT) means the mountlayer and regtest flips ride single byte-exact span patches, and the generalized chaining fix (a per-file working-text cache) lands as this round's engine self-patch for the future rounds that need it.

banner.title: THE MOUNTED-COMBAT ENGINE SITE - the R403 charge lands: the mount actor, the mounted resolution, and the charge closed
banner.provenance: The last ungated deferred item: the R403 mount layer consolidated six feeder seams and left the charge open because the engine had no mount actor. The site lands through the R774/R775 file-patch seam as five spec-declared patches: the Character mount field in game/party.h (0 = afoot, the v1-save default), the beginCombat mounted read in game/state_combat.cpp (the first living members riding report the company mounted - the combat open prints the riders), the rules/mountlayer.h contract flip (ONE span patch: the site exists, the charge closed), and the regtest.cpp R403 span flip (one byte-exact block carrying both conditions - the audit now fails if the site goes missing or the charge reopens). The state_combat TU is in the preflight build, so the site is compile-gated like every audit block. The mount field is a seam, not a save line: nothing writes mountKind yet (a later round may carry the saddle acquisition and the save line).
banner.sentinel: Zero book pages: the provenance is the engine site (the R403 seam closing against its already-landed feeders).

file_patches.note: the mount actor field lands on the Character
the mounted resolution seam opens at the combat open
the layer contract flips with the site (the site-exists bool flips true, the charge-open bool flips false - ONE span patch: one file, one patch this round)
the R403 audit follows the site: both charge conditions flip in one span (the RT patch is one byte-exact block - the engine chains one RT write, not many)

the engine chains: every patch on a file builds on the previous patch text (the multi-patch chaining class the R776 design exposed twice - two patches on one file lost the first flip to the stale re-read, RT and non-RT alike)
file_patches.from:
for fp in S.get('file_patches', []):
    p = fp['file']
    if not os.path.exists(p):
        die('the file patch target is '
            'missing: %s' % p)
    if p == RT:
        # RT is engine-patched in
        # memory (the include and
        # the audit); the file
        # patch rides that text,
        # never the pristine disk
        # copy (the clobber class:
        # the deferred writes would
        # lose the include and the
        # audit to the stale read)
        txt = rt
    else:
        txt = rd(p)
    if fp['to'] in txt:
        already.append('file: %s'
                       % fp['note'])
    else:
        if fp['from'] not in txt:
            die('the file patch anchor is '
                'missing: %s' % fp['note'])
        txt = txt.replace(fp['from'],
                          fp['to'], 1)
        writes.append((p, txt))
        applied.append('file: %s'
                       % fp['note'])
file_patches.to:
# the working texts: every patch
# on a file builds on the
# previous patch's text (the
# multi-patch chaining class: a
# file patched twice lost the
# first flip to the stale
# re-read - RT since R775, every
# other file since this fix)
fp_txt = {}
for fp in S.get('file_patches', []):
    p = fp['file']
    if p in fp_txt:
        txt = fp_txt[p]
    elif p == RT:
        # RT is engine-patched in
        # memory (the include and
        # the audit); the file
        # patch rides that text,
        # never the pristine disk
        # copy
        txt = rt
    else:
        if not os.path.exists(p):
            die('the file patch target '
                'is missing: %s' % p)
        txt = rd(p)
    if fp['to'] in txt:
        already.append('file: %s'
                       % fp['note'])
    else:
        if fp['from'] not in txt:
            die('the file patch anchor is '
                'missing: %s' % fp['note'])
        txt = txt.replace(fp['from'],
                          fp['to'], 1)
        fp_txt[p] = txt
        if p == RT:
            rt = txt
        writes.append((p, txt))
        applied.append('file: %s'
                       % fp['note'])
